items.title: How the SKA will use fast radio bursts to decode the universe
items.source: Astronomy News - Space News, Exploration News, Earth Science News, Earth Science
items.summary: There are parts of the universe that are extremely hard to see, even for our most advanced telescopes. Gas and dust don't emit light and are visible only by the light they block from stars and galaxies.

items.title: How supermassive black holes feed themselves
items.source: Astronomy News - Space News, Exploration News, Earth Science News, Earth Science
items.summary: Astronomers are closer to solving the mystery of how supermassive black holes feed themselves thanks to new images from the James Webb Space Telescope, or JWST.

items.title: Heavy-element exotic dust may solve a neutron star merger mystery
items.source: Astronomy News - Space News, Exploration News, Earth Science News, Earth Science
items.summary: When neutron stars merge, they create a powerful explosion called a kilonova that flings out neutron-rich material, some of which decays into heavy elements through a process called the r-process.

items.title: For time-critical events: NINJA prepares for first on-sky observations
items.source: Astronomy News - Space News, Exploration News, Earth Science News, Earth Science
items.summary: This summer, Subaru Telescope will welcome a new near-infrared spectrograph, NINJA, for its first on-sky engineering observations.

items.title: Are there aliens on exoplanet K2-18b? Scientists just scanned it for signals
items.summary: K2-18b is one of the most promising worlds for the search for extraterrestrial life, so astronomers conducted an unusually powerful radio survey using both the VLA and MeerKAT telescopes.

items.title: Frame-dragging observations validate Einstein yet again
items.source: Astronomy News - Space News, Exploration News, Earth Science News, Earth Science
items.summary: More than a century after Albert Einstein first transformed our understanding of gravity, his general theory of relativity continues to withstand ever more demanding experimental tests.
